Reconcile a dimensional breakdown against the line it breaks down

Source: R/check_breakdown.R
check_breakdown.Rd

Where a figure is reported both as a statement line and split across the members of a dimension – fixed assets by class, equity by reserve – the parts must add up to the whole. This checks that they do.

Usage

check_breakdown(x, by = NULL, period = "closing", tol = 1)

Arguments

x

A tibble from add_taxonomy(), read with dimensions = TRUE so that each dimension has its own column.

by

Columns identifying one statement instance. NULL, the default, uses whichever of file, basis and period the table has – file because read_xbrl() returns many filings at once, and without it two companies with the same balance sheet date are checked as one; add the company identifier for a panel.

period

"closing", the default, checks the year the filing declares for itself and leaves its comparative out – a comparative is usually partial, and its gaps are not the filing's. NULL checks every period the table carries.

tol

Absolute tolerance in the reporting currency. Default 1.

Value

A tibble with one row per element and dimension that is reported both ways: the by columns, elementid, label, dimension, line (the undimensioned figure), parts (the members summed), n_members, ratio and verdict – one of "agrees", "scaled by 1000", "scaled by 1/1000" or "parts do not cover the line".

Why it is worth checking separately

check_statement() follows the presentation hierarchy, which runs down the statement. A breakdown runs the other way, across a dimension, and nothing in the hierarchy reaches it. It is also where a particular error hides.

A filing in a sample of 300 Greenlandic companies tags its balance sheet in kroner and its fixed-asset note in thousands, in the same document. Its additions for the year read 229 and 174 when they are 229,000 and 174,000 kr, which would have entered an investment series at a thousandth of their size. Nothing else catches it: the unit is iso4217:DKK like every other filing's, decimals is consistent, and the company's registered capital clears its legal floor because the balance sheet is right. Only the note is wrong, and only the filing's own arithmetic shows it.

So the ratio is the point, not the difference. It is 1 when the breakdown agrees, 1000 or 0.001 when the two sit on different scales, and something near but not equal to 1 when the breakdown does not cover every member.

See also

check_statement() for the hierarchy, add_taxonomy().

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_cascade(), check_cashflow(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_report(), xbrl_report_data(), xbrl_resolve(), xbrl_robustness(), xbrl_screen(), xbrl_standardise(), xbrl_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
b <- check_breakdown(x)
b[b$verdict != "agrees", ]
} # }
